newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. signs bill to boost scrutiny of bonds.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. signs bill to boost scrutiny of bonds.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson has signed legislation designed to boost public scrutiny of local bond issues, a spokesman said on Friday.
The measure, by state Sen. Quentin Kopp, was introduced following the Orange County bankruptcy filing in December 1994. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June this year.

The legislation requires that any decision that involves the borrowing of $100,000 or more be considered as a separate item of business during regularly scheduled meetings of county supervisors and other local governing boards.

The measure states that the county treasurer serves as a trustee and a fiduciary with oversight responsibilities over funds deposited in the county treasury by other local government agencies, and that the county treasurer is subject to the prudent investor standard.
The measure also requires county supervisors to review and approve the annual investment policy of the county treasurer.

Proponents said the bill would provide added protection to the taxpayer since it requires local officials to discuss large bond issues separately in an open meeting. Its opponents said it would only prolong the community hearing process.

After filing for bankruptcy, Orange County supervisors were criticized for approving large borrowings as consent calendar items. The borrowings were included on a list of unrelated items that the county supervisors approved with a single vote and no discussion.
